entities.summary:
The Battle of Salsu, fought in 612 CE, was a pivotal encounter between the Eastern Turkish Göktürks and the Sui dynasty, taking place on the Ch'ongch'on River. This clash marked a significant turning point in the tumultuous relationship between the Göktürks and the Tang dynasty, which would shape the future of East Asia.

The battle, which occurred on the banks of the Ch'ongch'on River, saw the Göktürks emerge victorious, forcing the Sui dynasty to cede control of the region. The Sui dynasty, which had previously expanded its territories at the expense of the Göktürks, was now compelled to retreat. This reversal had far-reaching consequences, as it marked the beginning of a new era of tension between the Göktürks and the Tang dynasty.

The legacy of the Battle of Salsu can be seen in the subsequent rise of the Göktürks as a dominant force in East Asia, as well as the eventual collapse of the Sui dynasty. The Göktürks would go on to play a crucial role in shaping the politics and culture of the region for centuries to come.

As the Göktürk khagan (emperor) Bogu Yaghoучи succumbed to the Sui dynasty's relentless pressure, he was forced to retreat and regroup, marking a temporary setback for the Göktürks, but not a lasting one.
